facts.source: OCI Generative AI Enterprise AI Agents
facts.fact: Enterprise AI Agents are built two ways, which can be combined: the API-first OCI Responses API with OCI-managed tools, or hosted agentic applications (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).

An OCI Generative AI hosted agentic application is an "Application" (autoscaling, managed storage, VCN, endpoint auth) plus a "Deployment" that runs your container image (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).
An OCI Generative AI hosted agent Deployment runs a container image from OCI Container Registry (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).

The OCI Responses API supports four built-in tool types: `file_search` (vector stores), `code_interpreter` (Python in an OCI-managed container), `function` (client-executed) and `mcp` (remote MCP server) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).
The OCI Responses API `mcp` tool type calls a remote MCP server (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).
NL2SQL is not configured through the OCI Responses API `tools` parameter (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).

The OCI Responses API added xAI tools on 2026-05-29, background mode on 2026-07-29 and compaction via `POST /responses/compact` or `context_management` on 2026-10-27 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

An OCI Generative AI project groups responses, conversations, files, containers and sandboxes, and sets optional short-term memory compaction and optional long-term memory (an extraction model plus an embedding model) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI project response and conversation retention is at most 720 hours (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Neither OCI Generative AI project memory option (short-term compaction or long-term memory) can be disabled after creation without deleting the project (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).

facts.fact: OCI Generative AI sandboxes are available since 2026-10-20 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

OCI Generative AI sandboxes are temporary Linux workspaces for code and shell commands, scoped to a project and addressable by ID across workflow steps, with managed or custom outbound networking and optional warm pools (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI sandboxes can't be disabled after you enable them for a project (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

OCI Generative AI Enterprise AI NL2SQL generates SQL only, using a "semantic store" with two OCI Database Tools connections: an enrichment connection (higher privilege) and a query connection (lower privilege) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
NL2SQL-generated SQL is executed through the Database Tools MCP Server under the end user's identity (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
The default NL2SQL model is `openai.gpt-oss-120b` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
NL2SQL model selection, scheduled enrichment and background SQL generation were added on 2026-08-26 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

OCI Generative AI guardrails cover moderation, prompt injection, PII and topics; image moderation and guardrail version pinning were added in May 2026 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
OCI Generative AI guardrails are GA for on-demand since 2026-02-09 and for dedicated endpoints since 2026-02-26 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

Each OCI Generative AI routing profile names one on-demand model and target regions in the same realm and routes on-demand requests across them; routing profiles are available since 2026-09-23 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/routing-profile.htm).
"Global Generative AI availability" via routing profiles covers 30 OC1 regions since 2026-10-20 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
OCI Generative AI Agents, the older standalone service, is GA since 2024 and still documented separately (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/overview.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents provides managed agents with ready-to-use RAG, SQL and Agent (agent-as-a-tool) tools, custom Function Calling and custom API Endpoint Calling tools, and endpoints and sessions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/overview.htm).
The latest OCI Generative AI Agents release note is dated 2026-02-05 (routing-LLM model selection) (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai-agents/).

The OCI Agent Development Kit (ADK) is a client-side library for OCI Generative AI Agents released 2025-05-22 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai-agents/).

The OCI ADK ships in the OCI Python SDK as `oci.addons.adk`, installed with `pip install "oci[adk]"` and requiring Python 3.10+ (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/home.htm).
The OCI ADK ships in the OCI Java SDK as `bmc-addons/bmc-adk` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/home.htm).
The OCI ADK can attach MCP servers through `MCPClientStreamableHttp` / `MCPClientStdio` toolkits (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Oracle AI Database 26ai succeeds Oracle Database 23ai via the October 2025 release update, announced 2025-10-14 as a long-term support release that requires no upgrade or recertification from 23ai (https://blogs.oracle.com/database/oracle-announces-oracle-ai-database-26ai).
AI Vector Search is included in Oracle AI Database 26ai at no extra charge (https://blogs.oracle.com/database/oracle-announces-oracle-ai-database-26ai).

Oracle AI Database 26ai on-premises Linux x86-64 GA came with the January 2026 RU 23.26.1 (secondary for on-prem) (https://virtual-dba.com/blog/oracle-ai-database-26ai-now-available-for-linux-x86-64-on-premises/).
Oracle AI Vector Search uses the `VECTOR` data type, which requires `COMPATIBLE` >= 23.4.0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/26/vecse/overview-ai-vector-search.html).

Oracle AI Vector Search is exact or approximate (vector indexes), generates in-database embeddings with imported ONNX models, and ML algorithms accept `VECTOR` from 23.7 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/26/vecse/overview-ai-vector-search.html).

Oracle Autonomous AI Database 26ai replaces Autonomous Database 23ai; Oracle's rebranding release note names the service "Oracle Autonomous AI Database" (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/releasenotes/autonomous-database-dedicated/adbd-service-rebranding.htm).
Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse (Iceberg) was announced on 2025-10-14 (https://www.oracle.com/br/news/announcement/ai-world-oracle-introduces-autonomous-ai-lakehouse-2025-10-14/).

Select AI turns natural language into SQL in Autonomous AI Database, with actions `runsql`, `showsql`, `explainsql`, `narrate` and `chat` (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/dbms-cloud-ai-package.html).

Select AI uses AI profiles created with `DBMS_CLOUD_AI.CREATE_PROFILE` and activated per session with `DBMS_CLOUD_AI.SET_PROFILE` (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/dbms-cloud-ai-package.html).

Select AI providers include OCI Generative AI, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Cohere, Google, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Amazon Bedrock (`aws`) and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`provider_endpoint`) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-web/sdwad/create-ai-profile.html).
OCI Generative AI is one of the Select AI providers configured in an AI profile (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/dbms-cloud-ai-package.html).
Amazon Bedrock is a Select AI provider under the provider name `aws` (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/dbms-cloud-ai-package.html).

facts.fact: Select AI Agent is an in-database agent framework in package `DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT`: you build agents, tools, tasks and teams with `CREATE_AGENT`, `CREATE_TOOL`, `CREATE_TASK` and `CREATE_TEAM`, then run with `RUN_TEAM` or `SELECT AI agent` (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/getting-started-select-ai-agent.html).

Select AI Agent built-in tool types are SQL, RAG, WEBSEARCH and NOTIFICATION plus custom PL/SQL, and teams run in sequential or supervisor patterns (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/how-to-use-select-ai-supervisor-agent-teams.html).
Select AI Agent run history is in `USER_AI_AGENT_TEAM_HISTORY` and `USER_AI_AGENT_TASK_HISTORY` (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/getting-started-select-ai-agent.html).

Select AI Agent on Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata is dated 2026-02-03 in the dedicated release note describing the framework for agents, tools, tasks and teams (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/autonomous-database-dedicated/adbd-selectai-ragagent.htm).

Oracle Integration (OIC) agentic AI lets you register integrations in a project as "agentic AI tools" and build agents and agent patterns from a project AI tab (OIC 26.01) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).
Oracle Integration lets you enable a per-project MCP server for agentic AI tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).
A launch webcast for OIC agentic AI was scheduled for 2026-06-18 (secondary) (https://go.oracle.com/LP=152224).

facts.fact: OCI Data Science AI Quick Actions v2.0.1 is dated 2026-02-25 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/data-science/ai-quick-actions-201.htm).

OCI Functions, the serverless runtime for agent tools, is based on the Fn Project (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsinvokingfunctions.htm).
OCI Functions long-running "detached" invocations with success and failure destinations are GA (https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/longrunning-functions-and-response-destinations).

No dedicated OCI agent evaluation, tracing or computer-use or browser-use service was found in the Generative AI docs; the closest are Code Interpreter containers and sandboxes (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
Oracle Cost Advisor for AI has been in Limited Availability since 2026-10-27 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

OCI Generative AI's OpenAI-compatible base URL is `https://inference.generativeai.${region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai/v1` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/openai-compatible-api.htm).

The OCI Generative AI OpenAI-compatible API has paths `/responses`, `/conversations`, `/chat/completions`, `/files`, `/vector_stores/{id}/...` and `/containers` under `https://inference.generativeai.${region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai/v1` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/openai-compatible-api.htm).

No OpenAI-compatible embeddings path is listed for OCI Generative AI; embeddings and rerank use the OCI-native inference API (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/openai-compatible-api.htm).

An older OpenAI-compatible path under API version 20231130 is `https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/20231130/actions/v1/chat/completions` (Meta, xAI, gpt-oss) and `.../20231130/actions/v1/responses` (xAI, gpt-oss; not Meta) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
The OpenAI SDK has been supported against OCI Generative AI since 2025-11-05 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

The OCI Responses API requires a project OCID: pass `project="ocid1.generativeaiproject..."` in the OpenAI SDK, which sends the `OpenAI-Project` header (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).
The OCI Responses API `model` parameter is an on-demand model ID, a dedicated endpoint OCID, or a routing profile OCID (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).

OCI Generative AI API keys, available since 2026-01-21, are bearer secrets for the OpenAI-compatible endpoints sent as `Authorization: Bearer sk-...` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).

Each OCI Generative AI API key has two secrets with expirations (default three months) and is region-bound; IAM policies match keys with `request.principal.type='generativeaiapikey'` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
`oci generative-ai api-key create` (or the `CreateApiKey` operation) creates an OCI Generative AI API key (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
`oci-genai-auth` on PyPI is at v1.1.1 (2026-07-24) and needs Python >= 3.9 (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).

`oci-genai-auth` provides OCI IAM auth for the OpenAI SDK with classes `OciSessionAuth`, `OciUserPrincipalAuth`, `OciInstancePrincipalAuth` and `OciResourcePrincipalAuth`, passed as `httpx.Client(auth=...)` with `api_key="not-used"`; Oracle recommends it for production (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
`oci-genai-auth` supports instance principal auth via `OciInstancePrincipalAuth` (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).
`oci-genai-auth` supports resource principal auth via `OciResourcePrincipalAuth` (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).
`oci-genai-auth` supports session token auth via `OciSessionAuth` (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).

facts.fact: OCI Generative AI NL2SQL endpoints accept IAM-signed requests only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

NL2SQL semantic store CRUD is at `https://generativeai.${region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20231130/semanticStores` and Generate SQL is at `https://inference.generativeai.${region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20260325/semanticStores/{id}/actions/generateSqlFromNl` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI API keys are not accepted by NL2SQL endpoints (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

OCI Generative AI agents can call external MCP servers through the Responses API `mcp` tool, which takes `server_label`, `server_url`, `allowed_tools`, `require_approval` and `authorization` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/mcp.htm).

The Responses API `mcp` tool `authorization` value is a raw token without the `Bearer` prefix, which OCI says it does not store or log (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/mcp.htm).
Only Streamable HTTP is supported for MCP servers called from OCI Generative AI; SSE is deprecated and unsupported (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

OCI REST API request signing uses OCI Signature Version 1, based on draft-cavage-http-signatures-08 with `rsa-sha256` and `Authorization: Signature version="1",keyId="<tenancy_ocid>/<user_ocid>/<fingerprint>",...`; GET and DELETE sign `(request-target) host date`, and PUT and POST also sign `x-content-sha256`, `content-type` and `content-length` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/signingrequests.htm).
Clock skew over 5 minutes in OCI request signing returns `401 NotAuthenticated` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/signingrequests.htm).

`oci raw-request` signs arbitrary REST calls from the OCI CLI and is the Bash sample in the signing docs, alongside Python `oci.signer.Signer`, Java, TypeScript, Go, Ruby and C# samples (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/signingrequests.htm).

Official OCI SDKs exist for Python (`oci`), Java (`oci-java-sdk`), TypeScript/JavaScript (`oci-sdk`), .NET, Go (`github.com/oracle/oci-go-sdk`), Ruby, and PL/SQL (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdks.htm).
The OCI Python SDK (`oci`) is at v2.191.0, released 2026-11-10 (https://pypi.org/project/oci/).
A PL/SQL OCI SDK is preinstalled in Autonomous AI Database Serverless (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdks.htm).

`langchain-oci` is the LangChain integration for OCI Generative AI, providing `ChatOCIGenAI`, `OCIGenAIEmbeddings`, `OCIGenAIRerank` and `ChatOCIOpenAI` (Responses API), plus a `deepagents` extra with ADB and OpenSearch datastore tools (https://pypi.org/project/langchain-oci/).
`langchain-oci` v0.4.0 is dated 2026-10-21 (https://pypi.org/project/langchain-oci/).

The oracle/mcp GitHub repo is the official collection of local OCI MCP servers, with about 33 servers under `src/` including oci-cloud, oci-api, compute, networking, object-storage, identity, logging, monitoring, usage, pricing, limits, database, db-observability, faaas, registry, resource-search, support, mysql, oracle-data-studio, oracle-db-doc, goldengate and dbtools (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src).
The oracle/mcp README says "This repository is not intended for production use." (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).

`oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` is the recommended general-purpose OCI MCP server in oracle/mcp, run with `uvx oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server@latest` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

`oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` tools are `list_oci_clients`, `find_oci_api`, `describe_oci_operation`, `invoke_oci_api` and `list_client_operations` (SDK-backed) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

In stdio mode `oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` auth uses `OCI_CONFIG_FILE`, `OCI_CONFIG_PROFILE` and `OCI_MCP_AUTH_TYPE` (auto, api_key, security_token, instance_principal, resource_principal, oke_workload_identity and others) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

In HTTP mode `oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` auth uses an IDCS confidential app (`IDCS_DOMAIN`, `IDCS_CLIENT_ID`, scope `oci_mcp.cloud.invoke`) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

`oracle.oci-api-mcp-server` wraps the OCI CLI, runs with `uvx oracle.oci-api-mcp-server` (stdio only), and has tools `get_oci_command_help` and `run_oci_command` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-api-mcp-server).

`oracle.oci-api-mcp-server` blocks `--auth`, `--profile`, `--config-file`, `--endpoint` and `--proxy` overrides and runs with an empty `oci_cli_rc` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-api-mcp-server).
`dbtools-mcp-server` in oracle/mcp is a proof of concept as of 2026-11-14 (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/dbtools-mcp-server).

`dbtools-mcp-server` is a Python FastMCP server with 23 tools (list ADBs, run SQL via Database Tools connections, reports, `ragify_column`, HeatWave and Object Storage) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/dbtools-mcp-server).
`dbtools-mcp-server` reads `~/.oci/config` and runs with `python dbtools-mcp-server.py` (stdio) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/dbtools-mcp-server).

`oracle-db-doc-mcp-server` searches a locally built index of Oracle Database docs with its single tool `search_oracle_database_documentation` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oracle-db-doc-mcp-server).
A Docker image of `oracle-db-doc-mcp-server` is at `ghcr.io/oracle/mcp/oracle-db-doc` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oracle-db-doc-mcp-server).

The SQLcl MCP server is a local stdio server started with `sql -mcp` that uses SQLcl saved connections (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.2/sqcug/sqlcl-mcp-server-tools.html).

SQLcl MCP server tools are `list-connections`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `run-sql`, `run-sqlcl` and `schema-information` (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.2/sqcug/sqlcl-mcp-server-tools.html).

facts.fact: SQLcl MCP restrict levels are set with `-R <0-3>` in the client args (for example `["-R","1","-mcp"]`); the 25.4 docs say the default with no `-R` is level 4, the most restrictive (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/25.4/sqcug/configuring-restrict-levels-sqlcl-mcp-server.html).

A later SQLcl changelog says MCP startup now defaults to unrestricted, contradicting the 25.4 docs' level-4 default; that is the newer claim and the version of the change is unconfirmed (https://www.oracle.com/de/tools/sqlcl/sqlcl-changelog.html).

SQLcl MCP logs every request to the `DBTOOLS$MCP_LOG` table in the user's schema, and Oracle advises pruning it regularly (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-vscode/25.3/sqdnx/monitoring-sqlcl-mcp-server.html).
The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server is a managed remote MCP server, one per database, for 26ai and 19c (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server is GA, announced in release notes on 2025-12-23 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/autonomous-database-serverless/2025-12-mcp-server-for-autonomous-ai-database.htm).

The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server endpoint is `https://dataaccess.adb.{region}.oraclecloudapps.com/adb/mcp/v1/databases/{database-ocid}` over Streamable HTTP; a private-endpoint ADB uses a `hostname_prefix` URL reachable only from its VCN (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Enable the Autonomous AI Database MCP Server in the Console (database details, then Tool configuration, then Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, then Edit, then toggle); earlier docs used the free-form tag `adb$feature` = `{"name":"mcp_server","enable":true}` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Autonomous AI Database MCP Server auth options are OAuth dynamic client registration (`GET .../dcr_url` returns a randomized `/r/{random}` URL), static client registration by ADMIN (`POST .../adb/auth/v1/connect/databases/{ocid}/register`), or a bearer token (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

A bearer token for the Autonomous AI Database MCP Server comes from `POST .../adb/auth/v1/databases/{ocid}/token` (password grant with DB credentials, valid 1 hour) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Autonomous AI Database MCP Server tools are Select AI Agent tools: built-in tools plus custom tools registered with `DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT.CREATE_TOOL` over a PL/SQL function, listed in `USER_AI_AGENT_TOOLS` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).
Custom Autonomous AI Database MCP tools are registered with `DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT.CREATE_TOOL` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).
Autonomous AI Database MCP clients see only tools the DB user may use (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).
MLE JavaScript functions can't be Autonomous AI Database MCP tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

The Autonomous AI Database A2A Server publishes Select AI agent teams as A2A agents that clients discover through Agent Cards; it is a built-in, multi-tenant feature for 26ai and 19c on Serverless and Dedicated Region (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/agent2agent-protocol.html).
Autonomous AI Database A2A Server auth is OAuth using database credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/agent2agent-protocol.html).
The Autonomous AI Database A2A Server is enabled independently of the MCP Server (https://www.oracle.com/autonomous-database/a2a-server/).
The OCI Database Tools MCP Server, a managed MCP server for any Oracle AI Database in OCI, was introduced on 2026-05-12 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/database-tools/mcp.htm).

OCI Database Tools MCP Server auth is OAuth 2.0 through IAM identity domains (Personal Access Token or token-based), and the runtime identity is Resource Principal or Authenticated Principal (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/database-tools/doc/set-mcp-server.html).

The OCI Database Tools MCP Server exposes toolsets with built-in tools such as `run-sql` and reports, plus custom SQL and PL/SQL tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/database-tools/doc/set-mcp-server.html).
Invoking the OCI Database Tools MCP Server uses the IAM policy verb `use database-tools-mcp-servers-invocation` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/database-tools/doc/set-mcp-server.html).

The Database Tools MCP Server covers Autonomous AI Database, Base Database Service and Exadata Database Service through Database Tools connections at no incremental charge (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

The Database Tools MCP Server supports Base Database Service (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

The Database Tools MCP Server supports Exadata Database Service (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

The Database Tools MCP Server supports Autonomous AI Database, and a later release note added Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) support (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

Oracle Integration exposes one MCP server per project at `https://<instance>.integration.<region>.ocp.oraclecloud.com/mcp-server/v1/projects/<PROJECT_NAME>/mcp`, supporting `tools/list` and `tools/call`, in all OIC regions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).
Oracle Integration MCP server auth is OAuth 2.0 with OCI IAM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).

Calling the Oracle Integration MCP server needs a confidential app with the `ServiceInvoker` role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).

An OIC integration is an MCP tool only if it is in a project and Active, starts with a REST Adapter trigger using OAuth and a JSON payload, uses GET, POST, PUT, DELETE or PATCH, and is registered as an agentic AI tool (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).

facts.fact: OIC MCP can be configured in Fusion AI Agent Studio, where Streamable HTTP is recommended (secondary) (https://www.ateam-oracle.com/integrating-fusion-application-ai-agent-studio-with-oic-as-an-external-system).

OIC MCP configuration in AI Agent Studio does not support identity propagation (secondary) (https://www.ateam-oracle.com/integrating-fusion-application-ai-agent-studio-with-oic-as-an-external-system).

Google Gemini calls from OCI Generative AI leave OCI: they are served from Google locations (Americas, EU, Brazil or Asia-Pacific routing by region) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agentic-regions.htm).
xAI Grok calls from OCI Generative AI leave OCI because Grok is hosted by xAI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
OCI can reach Google through Oracle Interconnect for Google Cloud in Ashburn and Frankfurt (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

On Windows the OCI CLI MSI installer is downloaded from the oci-cli GitHub releases, bundles a compatible Python, and takes precedence over an existing non-MSI install (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/cliinstall.htm).
winget package `Oracle.OCI-CLI` (`winget install --id Oracle.OCI-CLI --exact`) is listed by third-party catalogs (secondary for winget) (https://winstall.app/apps/Oracle.OCI-CLI).

The OCI CLI PowerShell installer: run `Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`, then `iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/oci-cli/master/scripts/install/install.ps1'))`, or download the script and run `./install.ps1 -AcceptAllDefaults`; it installs Python if needed, and offline install is `install.ps1 -OfflineInstall` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/cliinstall.htm).

Install the OCI CLI via pip with `python -m venv oracle-cli`, `oracle-cli/Scripts/activate`, `pip install oci-cli` (or the release wheel `pip install oci_cli-*-py3-none-any.whl`), and verify with `oci --version` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/climanualinst.htm).
The current OCI CLI version is 3.96.2, released 2026-11-10 on GitHub (https://github.com/oracle/oci-cli/releases).

`oci setup config` creates an API-key profile via an interactive dialog that generates an RSA key pair and writes the config file; you then upload the public key in the Console, and `oci setup keys` generates keys only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/cliinstall.htm).

`oci session authenticate` creates a browser-based session token; commands then need `--auth security_token` or `OCI_CLI_AUTH=security_token` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clitoken.htm).

OCI session tokens last 1 hour by default and can be refreshed with `oci session refresh --profile

` for up to 24 hours; headless options are `--no-browser` (5 to 60 minutes) and `oci session export` / `oci session import` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clitoken.htm).

The OCI config file default path is `~/.oci/config`; on Windows PowerShell it is `$Env:UserProfile\.oci\config` (`C:\Users\<user>\.oci\config`) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdkconfig.htm).

OCI config file entries are `user`, `fingerprint`, `key_file`, `tenancy` and `region`, plus `security_token_file` for session auth (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdkconfig.htm).

OCI CLI environment variables include `OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE`, `OCI_CLI_PROFILE`, `OCI_CLI_AUTH` (`api_key`, `instance_principal`, `resource_principal`, `security_token`, `instance_obo_user`), `OCI_CLI_REGION`, `OCI_CLI_RC_FILE`, `OCI_CLI_KEY_CONTENT` and `OCI_CLI_SECURITY_TOKEN_FILE`; precedence is command option, then env var, then config file (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clienvironmentvariables.htm).
The OCI CLI accepts `OCI_CLI_AUTH=instance_principal` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clienvironmentvariables.htm).
The OCI CLI accepts `OCI_CLI_AUTH=resource_principal` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clienvironmentvariables.htm).

OCI CLI command groups for agent work are `generative-ai`, `generative-ai-inference`, `generative-ai-data` (NL2SQL), `generative-ai-sandbox`, `generative-ai-agent`, `generative-ai-agent-runtime`, `db` (includes `db autonomous-database`), `dbtools`, `dbtools-runtime`, `fn`, `api-gateway`, `data-science`, `integration` and `resource-manager` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/tools/oci-cli/latest/oci_cli_docs/).

The OCI CLI manages OCI Generative AI through the `generative-ai`, `generative-ai-inference`, `generative-ai-data` and `generative-ai-sandbox` command groups (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/tools/oci-cli/latest/oci_cli_docs/).

`oci fn function invoke` is the production invoke path for OCI Functions; it supports `--fn-invoke-type detached` and its sync timeout is `--read-timeout` (default 60 s) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsinvokingfunctions.htm).
The Fn Project CLI `fn invoke` is recommended for development only when invoking OCI Functions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsinvokingfunctions.htm).
The Terraform OCI provider (`oracle/oci`) latest version is v9.13.0, released 2026-11-11 (https://github.com/oracle/terraform-provider-oci/releases).

Recent Terraform OCI provider Generative AI additions are model discovery and routing profiles (v9.3.0, 2026-09-24), GenAI API key support (v9.9.0, 2026-10-06) and bring-your-own reservations for dedicated AI clusters (v9.11.0, 2026-10-21) (https://github.com/oracle/terraform-provider-oci/releases).

The Terraform OCI provider has Gen AI Agents resources such as `oci_generative_ai_agent_agent` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/tools/terraform-provider-oci/7.23.0/docs/r/generative_ai_agent_agent.html).

Meta Llama 4 on-demand on OCI Generative AI is Chicago only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

Use a routing profile from OCI regions without local Generative AI processing (for example Sydney) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
An OCI Generative AI API key must be in the same region as the model and works only for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
OCI Generative AI NL2SQL requires IAM auth and does not accept API keys (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI dedicated-mode model retirement is later than on-demand retirement (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deprecating-dedicated.htm).
Cohere Embed English 3 retires in OCI Generative AI dedicated mode on 2026-09-30 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deprecating-dedicated.htm).
Cohere Embed 4 is the replacement for Cohere Embed English 3 on OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deprecating-dedicated.htm).
OCI Notifications alert subscribers 14 and 7 days before an OCI Generative AI on-demand model retirement (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/retire-announcements.htm).
Cohere aliases `cohere.command-latest` and `cohere.command-plus-latest` were removed from OCI Generative AI on 2026-07-30 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
The OCI Generative AI GenerateText API was deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).
The OCI Generative AI SummarizeText API was deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).
The OCI Generative AI Chat API replaces the GenerateText API, deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).
The OCI Generative AI Chat API replaces the SummarizeText API, deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents (older service) adjustable limit defaults are `agent-count` 2, `knowledge-base-count` 3, `agent-endpoint-per-agent-count` 3 and `session-per-agent-endpoint-count` 1,000 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/limits.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents (older service) fixed limits: tools per agent are 20 in FRA, LHR and ORD but 5 in IAD, GRU and KIX; data source files are 100 MB max; user messages are 24,000 characters max; session idle timeout is 1 hour to 7 days (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/limits.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents (older service) regions are `us-ashburn-1`, `sa-saopaulo-1`, `eu-frankfurt-1`, `ap-osaka-1`, `uk-london-1`, `us-chicago-1` and `us-phoenix-1` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/overview.htm).

OCI Functions sync timeout defaults to 30 s (max 300 s), detached invocation allows 5 to 3,600 s, memory is 128 to 3,072 MB, and request and response payloads are fixed at 6 MB (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionscustomizing.htm).

OCI API Gateway request bodies are limited to 20 MB, HTTP backend read and send timeouts default to 10 s (configurable 1 to 300 s), and method, URI and headers are capped at 8 KB combined (https://docs.cloud.oracle.com/iaas/Content/APIGateway/Reference/apigatewaylimits.htm).
OCI API Gateway allows only 6 MB for a Functions backend, and a larger function response returns 502 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/changes/eca7dd82-d5ae-44e5-a574-03c4563e10a7).
Autonomous AI Database MCP bearer tokens expire after 1 hour (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Changing an Autonomous AI Database MCP tool requires drop and recreate, and clients must reconnect to see the change (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Autonomous AI Database MCP clients must support remote Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1 or token auth; in Oracle's example Claude Desktop needs the `mcp-remote` bridge (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/prerequisites.html).
